# [TASK] Facade hardening: TTL/growth policy + single-flight for concurrent misses

## Task
Two real gaps in the TMDB facade's caching, now that ADR-010 replaced the
raw-passthrough model with one mapped `Movie` collection:

- **List/search endpoints have no single-flight.**
  `MovieService.getOrFetchMovieEntity` (movie-detail path) already guards
  concurrent misses with a `ReentrantLock`. The list/search methods
  (`discoverMoviesRaw`, `searchMoviesRaw`, `getMovieCategoryRaw`, etc.) are
  `@Cacheable(value = "movieLists")` without `sync = true`, so concurrent
  misses on the same list key can each call TMDB.
- **No growth policy for the persisted `Movie` catalog.** Every
  list-endpoint call upserts its results, so the collection grows
  unbounded with no TTL, expiry, or cleanup policy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] List/search facade methods in `MovieService` (`discoverMoviesRaw`,
      `searchMoviesRaw`, `getMovieCategoryRaw`, and siblings) get
      single-flight protection for concurrent cache misses (e.g.
      `@Cacheable(sync = true)` or a per-key lock)
- [x] A real multi-threaded test (actual concurrent calls, not sequential
      mock calls) against WireMock proves N concurrent misses on the same
      key produce exactly 1 upstream TMDB call — covering both a detail
      endpoint and a list endpoint
- [x] A growth/retention policy for the persisted `Movie` catalog is
      decided and implemented (e.g. TTL index or scheduled cleanup
      differentiating list-sourced vs. detail-sourced documents)
- [x] The decision and final state are documented (ADR update or code
      comment)

## Estimate
**Hours:** 6

## Notes
Builds on `MovieService`'s existing `ReentrantLock` single-flight for detail misses — already correct, but untested for real concurrency and not extended to list endpoints.

The original `tmdb_raw_documents` growth policy is stale: that collection no longer exists. ADR-010 redirects it at the `Movie` collection. See ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4 and ADR-010 (which supersedes ADR-003).

Done in commit `cfbda14`: `sync = true` on every list/search `@Cacheable` method, and `MovieCatalogRetentionService` purging list-sourced stubs daily (`movie.catalog.retention-days`, default 7). `MovieServiceConcurrencyTest` proves exactly one upstream TMDB call under 10 concurrent threads for both a detail and a list endpoint.

This was implemented before the issue was first closed but never committed — reclosed now that the code exists.
